rescore_reason: Orchestrator assigned Slice B at 5 apples for FULL parity (13-stage pipeline, 30+ mutating actions, ~930-line queue state machine, Azure generation). Investigation showed full write-parity is not viable in one clean PR; flagged the split to the orchestrator. This PR ships ONLY the read/browse surface (backlog dashboard with confirmed-real integration column, plan/brief YAML viewers, run inspection) with zero mutations, no state-machine port, and no Azure calls — after an orchestrator scope refinement (2026-07-09) moved the read-only durable-queue + asset-request status reads into B2 (a status read without its start/stop/mutate controls is a confusing half-panel, so each pairs with its mutations in B2). B2 (all writes: synthesize/promote/generate/postprocess/judge/approve/checkin/metadata/tag + worker/issues start-stop + queue state machine + the two status reads) is a documented follow-up. The shipped read slice is honestly a 3-apple change.

plan_review.notes: Separate-model (gpt-5.4) rubber-duck plan review. 2 blocking + 5 important + 2 nice-to-have, all addressed. BLOCKING-1 (unverified integration): added an explicit unverified path in workflow-model - when the sprite/item registry cannot be loaded (integrationResolved=false), target-bearing assets get integrationState='unverified' and approved+file-present assets get status='approved-unverified' rather than a fabricated 'missing'; renderer shows a banner. The ported resolveIntegrationState/resolveArtPlanStatus stay byte-1:1 with the monolith (overlay is additive, behind an option defaulting to the monolith behavior). BLOCKING-2 (durable queue read omitted): pulled the read-only GET /api/workflow/state into B1 as a faithful read-only queue table (items: seq/name/kebabName/type/stage/source + raw-JSON details); narrowed the B1 claim to read/browse parity (explicitly NOT the interactive queue state machine, which stays B2). IMPORTANT-1 (asset-requests read): pulled read-only GET /api/workflow/asset-requests into B1. IMPORTANT-2: added normalizeAssetPath (strip leading slash and 'assets/') before the fs existence check. IMPORTANT-3 (path traversal): plan/brief content is served ONLY via an allowlist map built from listArtPlans/listBriefs (relPath -> absPath); arbitrary query params are never path.join'd against repoRoot. IMPORTANT-4 (perf): per-instance cache of backlog + registryIds + allowlist, recomputed only on explicit reload; live sidecar reads stay per-buildState. IMPORTANT-5 (store-oriented runs): each run carries a best-effort 'promoted' flag derived from matching its runId against manifest sourceRun tails, plus a client-side All/Promoted/Unpromoted filter. NICE-1 (cache namespace): the vendored image-cache is already per-extension and runIds are globally-unique timestamps+hashes, so cross-worktree collision is effectively impossible; vendored file left unchanged. NICE-2: added renderer/state degrade tests (sidecar down, wrong-repo, unverified integration). SCOPE REFINEMENT (post-plan-review, orchestrator-directed 2026-07-09): the read-only durable-queue read (BLOCKING-2) and asset-requests read (IMPORTANT-1) were subsequently moved OUT of B1 into the B2 write slice — a status read without its start/stop/mutate controls is a confusing half-panel, so each pairs with its mutations in B2. Final B1 = 3 self-contained read surfaces (backlog, plan/brief browsing, run inspection). The BLOCKING-2 concern itself (never fabricate integration status) remains fully addressed via the unverified path, which now shipped as confirmed-real (24 sprites + 123 items via esbuild source-transform, degrade is fallback-only).

rounds.notes: Round 1 (single-model code-review agent) on the pre-trim 5-surface shape. Verified 8 invariants concretely: async getStatic awaited at every call site; plan/brief content served ONLY via an allowlist Map keyed by relPath (never path.join(repoRoot,userInput)); REPO_ROOT via path.resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath),'..','..','..') not session.workspacePath; no console.* (session.log/log() only); graceful sidecar degrade; imageCache.fetchThrough hit/miss contract; run-selection state machine; and a 1:1 port of resolveIntegrationState/resolveArtPlanStatus/briefKey vs src/shared/art-plan-status.ts. Re-ran the registry loader live (24 sprites + 123 items, error=null). Verdict: no blocking/important concerns. Marked clean:false because the reviewed diff was then materially changed by the scope trim (Queue+Requests read tabs removed), necessitating round 2 on the final shape.

Round 2 (single-model code-review agent) on the FINAL trimmed diff after the orchestrator scope refinement removed the Queue (workflow-state) + Requests (asset-requests) read tabs into B2. Verified: ZERO dangling references to removed symbols (renderQueue/renderRequests/safeJson/fetchWorkflowState/fetchAssetRequests/workflowStateUrl/assetRequestsUrl/get_workflow_state/get_asset_requests and queue/requests tab ids all gone; 'queue' survives only in B2-prose comments + the base-harness 'queueBackend' /api/health field, distinct from the removed tab); the run-selection state machine (entry.requested briefId/runId) is intact and untouched; all 8 invariants from round 1 still hold; sidecar-client return object + urls object have no leftover workflowState/assetRequests entries while runsUrl(baseUrl,{promoted}) base code is retained; tests/sidecar-client.test.mjs rewritten to cover only the retained surface (runsUrl incl promoted, runSummaryUrl/sheetUrl/sliceMapUrl encoding, listRuns via fake fetchImpl) and still exercises the ../../../../scripts/shared import-resolution; renderer.test.mjs asserts Queue/Requests renderers are ABSENT; 28/28 ext tests pass incl harness-drift. ONE non-blocking concern: a stale 'all five read surfaces' docstring in renderer.test.mjs:4 — FIXED to 'all three' (comment-only). Loop converged clean within the 2-round cap; no human escalation needed.

Round 3 adjudicates the 15 automated review threads raised by copilot-pull-request-reviewer on the open PR (#990). Each was evaluated against the canonical source before acting (rule #12 — never blind-resolve); all 15 were genuine (cosmetic → security-hardening), all fixed: [4][5] get_plan/get_brief actions did readFileSync with NO try/catch while the GET fileContentRoute wrapped it — wrapped both action handlers to throw a controlled CanvasError('read_failed'), matching the route's graceful degrade. [6][10] registry-ids loadIdSet imported esbuild twice via `(await import).default ?? (await import)` — import once into esbuildMod, then pick .default ?? namespace. [7] renderer client STATUS_ORDER put approved-unverified mid-list, contradicting the domain model's ALL_STATUSES (which appends the canvas-only degrade status LAST) — moved it last to match. [8][9] yaml-reader walkFiles used dirent flags then fell back to statSync (FOLLOWS symlinks), so a repo-controlled symlink under plans/ or briefs/ could escape repoRoot and disclose arbitrary files — now skips entry.isSymbolicLink() and uses lstatSync (never follows) in the defensive fallback. [14] workflow-model promotedRunIds keyed by only the last path segment (runId) via split('/').pop(); the canonical sidecar (server.ts listPromotedRuns, 2460-2468) backslash-normalizes and keys by the last TWO segments (<briefId>/<runId>) — aligned the model to `.replace(/\\/g,'/')` + slice(-2) + `${briefId}/${runId}`, and the run-list consumer (extension.mjs) now matches by `${run.briefId}/${run.runId}`. Added a Windows-backslash regression test (loadBacklog normalizes runs\enemy-orc\... → enemy-orc/...) and hardened the existing test to assert the runId-alone key is absent. [1][2][3][11][12][13] stale 'sprite-review' @module tags + hop-path comment in the vendored yaml-reader.mjs/sidecar-client.mjs (NOT drift-tested — CANONICAL_FILES is only canvas-harness.mjs+image-cache.mjs) → retagged workflow/*. [15] tests/registry-ids.test.mjs comment 'Three hops' → 'Four hops' (code does four `..`). During the fix pass the ext test suite caught a real bug I introduced — a backtick around 'approved-unverified' in a renderer comment that sits inside a backtick template literal, which prematurely closed the client-script string (SyntaxError) — fixed to plain text. Final: 29/29 ext tests pass (was 28; +1 Windows-path test). Loop converged clean; no human escalation needed.
